item.title: Women record more online abuse than men, with 585 complaints received this year - Online Safety Commission
item.description: Speaking during a panel discussion on technology-facilitated gender-based violence in political life, Online Safety Commission representative Joshua Singh says the figures indicate that women continue to be targeted online despite ongoing awareness programmes. item.content:encoded:
Speaking during a panel discussion on technology-facilitated gender-based violence in political life, Online Safety Commission representative Joshua Singh says the figures indicate that women continue to be targeted online despite ongoing awareness programmes.

He says 946 complaints were received from women in 2025 compared to 658 from men, while in 2024, 830 complaints were received from women compared to 541 from men.

Singh says women in politics and public office can be particularly exposed to online abuse because they hold positions of influence and speak publicly on issues that may attract strong reactions.

Insert: Singh on women. 22nd September, 26

He says people need to know how to protect themselves online, including blocking users, deleting abusive comments and reporting harmful content.

Singh says the Online Safety Commission can also assist people in getting harmful images, videos and comments removed from social media and other online platforms.

He says this includes cases where artificial intelligence has been used to alter or create images of people without their consent.

Singh says the Commission can also refer cases to the Police where it believes the matter meets the threshold for prosecution.

He says removing harmful content can take time, with requests to online platforms sometimes taking several days to be acted on.

Singh made the comments during the Women's Political Participation programme on confronting technology-facilitated gender-based violence.

item.title: Savusavu residents to raise climate concerns directly with Kamikamica at FMA Town Hall
item.description: Savusavu residents will have the chance to put their concerns directly to Deputy Prime Minister Manoa Kamikamica when he will attend the Fijian Media Association Public Town Hall Forum on climate change and environmental issues today. The Pre-COP31 Climate Change Town Hall Forum will be held at Nukubalavu Village in Savusavu from 7pm to 9.30pm tomorrow.
item.content:encoded:
Savusavu residents will have the chance to put their concerns directly to Deputy Prime Minister Manoa Kamikamica when he will attend the Fijian Media Association Public Town Hall Forum on climate change and environmental issues today.

The Pre-COP31 Climate Change Town Hall Forum will be held at Nukubalavu Village in Savusavu from 7pm to 9.30pm tomorrow.

The forum, organised by the FMA, will give residents an opportunity to raise concerns about environmental and climate challenges affecting their communities, question Government action and propose practical solutions.

Kamikamica will be joined by Permanent Secretary for the Ministry of Environment Dr Sivendra Michael, other Government officials and experts from regional agencies who will be in Savusavu for the PINA Media Summit.

The discussion will be moderated by fijivillage News Director Vijay Narayan and Fiji Television Manager News Stella Taoi.

Residents are encouraged to share their own experiences, including changes they have observed, challenges affecting their livelihoods and solutions they believe should receive greater attention.

Questions around Government responses and the support needed by communities will also form part of the discussion.

The forum will be livestreamed across participating media platforms, including fijivillage.

It will be held alongside the 8th Pacific Media Summit, hosted by the Fijian Media Association and the Pacific Islands News Association.

The town hall is aimed at bringing community voices into the regional gathering of Pacific journalists and media leaders, while creating a direct platform for public discussion and accountability on climate and environmental issues.

The event is supported by PACMAS and forms part of the Fijian Media Association’s collaborative town hall initiative involving Fiji’s media organisations.

Residents of Savusavu and surrounding communities are being invited to attend and take part in the discussion.

item.title: Market vendor safety boosted with $146,343 worth of CCTV and PA systems
item.description: Market vendors, especially women, will have safer and more secure workplaces with the handover of CCTV cameras and public address systems to eight municipal councils. The equipment, worth $146,343 .47 , was handed over under the Markets for Change programme to strengthen security, improve communication and enable faster responses to incidents in municipal markets.
item.content:encoded:
Market vendors, especially women, will have safer and more secure workplaces with the handover of CCTV cameras and public address systems to eight municipal councils.

The equipment, worth $146,343 .47 , was handed over under the Markets for Change programme to strengthen security, improve communication and enable faster responses to incidents in municipal markets.

UN Women Fiji Multi-Country Office Deputy Representative Eri Taniguchi says women spend a large part of their day in markets, connecting with other vendors, accessing information and services and supporting one another.

Taniguchi says when markets are not safe, women's livelihoods, well-being and opportunities can be affected, with concerns such as theft, violence and harassment making it harder for women to work and participate fully in economic life.

She says creating safer markets is therefore not only about security, but also about creating an environment where women can work, do business and participate with confidence and dignity.

The handover follows the Memorandum of Understanding on Safer Markets signed in October last year by the Fiji Police Force, municipal councils and the Market Vendors Association, with support from IFAD and UN Women.

Australian Deputy High Commissioner Elizabeth Petrovic says women make up between 70 and 85 percent of market vendors in Fiji.

Petrovic says vendors need to feel safe, while customers, families and communities also need to trust that markets are safe places.

She says the Australian Government is proud to provide the support requested by the Fijian Government and to partner in strengthening safety in markets.

Petrovic says the handover includes 50 CCTV cameras, eight LED display screens and public announcement systems.

She says the equipment is expected to make a practical difference for market vendors and help create markets that are safer, more welcoming and more resilient.

Local Government Minister Maciu Nalumisa says CCTV cameras can act as a deterrent and also assist in investigations.

He says the equipment will not only assist vendors and municipal councils but will also support the Fiji Police Force in creating safer communities and marketplaces.

Nalumisa says the municipal councils receiving the equipment should use the systems proactively, integrate them into their operations and emergency plans and coordinate the cameras with police operations.

He also addressed concerns about surveillance and privacy, saying the systems are intended to protect public spaces, assist in detecting crime and provide timely information during emergencies.

Nalumisa says strict operational guidelines will be put in place to ensure transparency and accountability.

item.title: 10 years later, Miss Hibiscus returns to Holy Trinity to inspire next generation
item.description: Her visit also highlighted a school project, aimed at providing students with a safe place to wait for their parents and other transport after school. Korosaya attended Holy Trinity from Year 1 to Year 8 and was also head girl and dux of the school.
item.content:encoded:
Her visit also highlighted a school project, aimed at providing students with a safe place to wait for their parents and other transport after school.

Korosaya attended Holy Trinity from Year 1 to Year 8 and was also head girl and dux of the school.

She says returning to the school brought back memories of being a young student preparing to enter high school and begin the next stage of her education.

Korosaya encouraged young girls at the school to believe they are capable of achieving anything they put their minds to.

Insert:Korosaya on young girls. 23rd Sep, 26

She says leadership and change can begin in their homes, communities and classrooms.

Korosaya says this includes taking on leadership roles, being willing to learn and having the confidence to say, “I can do it.”

She says parents, teachers and communities also have an important role in supporting young women to become successful future leaders and citizens.

Korosaya is also encouraging former Holy Trinity students to return for the school's Yellow Note Day this Saturday, give back to the school and reconnect with former classmates.

Meanwhile, Holy Trinity Anglican School Principal Johnson Rura says the school is working to complete a mini pavilion that will accommodate around 500 to 600 students.

Rura says the idea for the facility dates back 34 years and comes from the need for a proper place where students can safely wait for their parents and other transport after school.

He says the project is being funded by the school's Parents and Teachers Association and parents, with assistance from Republic of Fiji Military Forces engineers.

Rura says more funds are needed to complete the project.

He is inviting former students, teachers and supporters of the school to attend its annual fundraising bazaar on October 31 to help raise money for the pavilion.

Rura says Korosaya was invited back to spend time with the students and inspire them, particularly those in Year 8.
